cases.estimand: One ordered fixation-summary group per declared trial key.
conventions: onset and duration use caller-supplied units
eye_table clips to bounds before grouping
eyes4s must account for every accepted or rejected input row
cases.independent_case: Row ids valid-a, outside-left and zero-duration distinguish clipping from explicit row/trial rejection.
cases.divergence: Valid coordinates and explicit times agree. eyesim clips outside and NA positions, accepts zero durations, duplicate/unsorted fixations and closed upper bounds, errors on empty groups, and reclassifies arbitrary tables. eyes4s uses half-open geometry and positive intervals, explicit ordinal order and whole-trial quarantine with every rejected source row retained. Coordinate conversion is an explicit Warp, not an import default.

cases.estimand: A declared map from one spatial coordinate system to another, applied to fixation coordinates; the affine is determined by the three fitting pairs alone and checked on the excluded held-out point.
conventions: no axis flip: every eyes4s target frame declares the source y-axis
coordinate normalization is distinct from mass normalization
held-out point is excluded from fitting
absolute tolerance 1e-12; 1e-9 for the floating-point solve
cases.independent_case: An exact rational oracle applies every supplied map, solves the affine from the three training pairs without the held-out point, and records axis-swap and no-translation mutants that miss the held-out target; eyesim has no coordinate affine entry point, so the affine targets are oracle-only.

cases.estimand: Component-wise ordered scanpath similarity after monotone alignment, optionally within a time window.
conventions: eyesim exposes a sixth order-insensitive EMD component
cases.independent_case: Three-point paths on a 100 by 50 screen distinguish direction, length, position and duration normalization.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned eyesim fixture reconciled separately from the existing Python implementation conformance.

cases.estimand: Order-insensitive fixation-pattern transport or proportion of sampled trajectory positions within a spatial threshold.
conventions: Sinkhorn is a divergence-shaped comparison, not a metric
cases.independent_case: The selected paths cross the distance threshold between query times and distinguish interpolation from fixation-only matching.
cases.planned_evidence: Reference outputs for both overlap metrics and a dependency-locked Sinkhorn case.

cases.estimand: A weighted Gaussian intensity or normalized mass evaluated on an explicit rectangular grid.
conventions: duration_weighted default differs by entry point
cases.independent_case: A 5 by 3 non-square grid with reversed explicit weights detects axis, weighting, normalization and edge-policy mistakes.
cases.planned_evidence: Separate ks and MASS locks plus an analytic Gaussian small-grid oracle.

cases.estimand: Interpolated surface value at each requested fixation coordinate.
conventions: evaluation is deterministic and is not random sampling
output cardinality matches query cardinality or reports failures
cases.independent_case: Two inside and two outside queries distinguish interpolation, clipping and partial indexing.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned point values and explicit outside-domain results for every normalization.

methods: duration-proportional row replication at a temporal resolution
density lookup along the sampled trajectory (sample_density with times)
cases.estimand: The fixation position in force at each requested time, the rows implied by each fixation's duration at a stated temporal resolution, and the template-density value at the sampled positions. Every output is a deterministic function of its inputs; eyesim draws nothing at random here.
conventions: a time before the first onset is NA on both paths
after the last onset the fast path returns NA while the slow path holds the last fixation
neither path consults duration, so a gap between fixations keeps the preceding position
equal onsets are averaged by the fast path and resolved to the later row by the slow path
rep_fixations repeats each row as.integer(duration / (1 / resolution)) times, truncating and never fewer than once
sample_density returns NA wherever the sampled trajectory is NA
requested and realized cardinality both retained
eyes4s_public_api: a time-indexed Scanpath lookup is planned
cases.independent_case: A two-fixation path queried before its first onset, at and between onsets, after the last onset and after the last fixation ends separates the fast and slow endpoint policies from a duration-aware lookup; a duration of 0.29 at resolution 100, 29 steps in exact arithmetic, exposes the floating-point truncation to 28 rows; a duplicated onset exposes the averaging.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned fast and slow sample_fixations, rep_fixations and sample_density-with-times output on a declared path, an independent step-function oracle, and an eyes4s public route that evaluates a scanpath at requested times with explicit out-of-support results.

cases.estimand: Shannon entropy of a supplied non-negative map after sum-normalisation, optionally divided by the log of the cell count.
conventions: normalize default true divides by the log of the count of finite cells, which is the cell count on a positive map
an unnormalised count map is sum-normalised first
the eye_density and density methods are the same routine
cases.independent_case: A 60-digit decimal oracle of the Shannon entropy of mass_p (exactly 1.5 bits), the uniform mass_q (maximal) and the all-positive mass_r in both bases, raw and relative, computed without either implementation; the count map [2, 1, 1, 0] must give mass_p's entropy.

cases.estimand: Entropy of a map derived from a fixation group by KDE or by occupancy-grid counts, and the mean or per-scale vector over a multiscale object.
conventions: suggest_sigma default bandwidth when sigma is NULL
padded observed bounds when none are supplied
grid counts use findInterval with the rightmost cell closed
cases.independent_case: The density method depends on the unresolved KDE row; the grid method and the multiscale mean/none reductions can be pinned on the entropy lattice with the explicit scale weights [1, 3].
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned fixation_group grid-method and multiscale mean/none output with explicit weights, and density-method output once the KDE row is settled.

cases.estimand: The cell-wise two-map mean and the cell-wise difference of two maps on one lattice.
conventions: identical lattices required; a shifted lattice is an error in both
+ is the two-map mean (e1 + e2) / 2, not a sum
- is a signed map: eyesim classes it eye_density_delta, eyes4s types it Signed
cases.independent_case: Exact rational mean and difference of mass_p and mass_q; the difference sums to zero and goes negative at mass_p's zero cell, so a sum masquerading as a mean or a dropped sign is visible.

cases.estimand: The natural-log ratio of two maps cell by cell; neither implementation has a product.
conventions: eyesim applies no floor: a zero numerator gives -Inf, a zero denominator Inf, both zero NaN
eyes4s floors both cells at 1e-12 by default and refuses a non-finite Signed map when floor = 0
* stops with undefined operation in eyesim and does not typecheck in eyes4s
absolute tolerance 1e-12 away from zero cells
cases.independent_case: 60-digit decimal log ratios of mass_r over mass_q (no zero cell) and of mass_p over mass_q away from the zero cell; the floored eyes4s value at the zero cell, log(1e-12 / 0.25), is computed from the same rationals.
cases.divergence: At a zero cell eyesim returns -Inf, Inf or NaN and keeps the result classed as a density; eyes4s floors both cells at 1e-12 so the Signed map stays finite, records the floor in provenance, and refuses the unfloored infinity as NonFiniteValue. Away from zero cells the two agree to 1e-12. Neither has a product.

methods: entropy of an exact difference map
entropy of a signed map with positive total
cases.estimand: What each implementation answers when a signed map is offered where a probability mass is expected.
conventions: eyesim keeps operator results classed eye_density, so fixation_entropy accepts them
entropy_from_mass drops non-finite cells, divides by the signed total, sums positive cells only, and returns NA when the total is within .Machine$double.eps of zero
eyes4s Mass and Intensity reject a negative cell with NegativeValue; Signed has no entropy
cases.independent_case: The exact difference mass_p - mass_q has total zero; the signed vector [0.5, -0.25, 0.75, 0] has total one and positive cells summing to 1.25; the log-ratio map has one -Inf cell. A labelled reading of eyesim's formula reproduces its pinned finite value -(0.5 ln 0.5 + 0.75 ln 0.75).
cases.divergence: eyesim returns NA for the exact difference map, a finite 0.5623 nats for the signed vector (its positive cells over the signed total, not the entropy of anything), exactly 0 for the log-ratio map after dropping its -Inf cell, and NA for the NaN-bearing p / p map. eyes4s refuses at the type (entropy is defined on Mass only; the suite uses typeCheckErrors) and at construction (NegativeValue names the offending cell). The eyesim values are pinned so the refusal is evidenced, not asserted.

cases.estimand: The named association, similarity or distance on common spatial support; multiscale results retain scale before any explicit mean.
conventions: multiscale supports all listed methods except emd at the pinned revision
cases.independent_case: Nonconstant, constant and zero four-cell vectors expose undefined correlations, zero norms and scale-direction mistakes.
cases.planned_evidence: One pinned and one independent case for every method and failure boundary.

cases.estimand: For each recall trial, cosine to the same-participant same-image encoding trial minus the mean cosine to all other images for that participant.
conventions: three candidates yield one match and two controls
cases.independent_case: An exact rational oracle enumerates all eighteen pairs and six reductions without calling either implementation.

cases.estimand: The same matched/control query with every focal key and failure outcome retained.
conventions: undefined constant Pearson is a value
diagnostics name focal and reference operands
cases.independent_case: Composite-key truth tables and the correlation formula justify the eyes4s behavior independently of both implementations.
cases.divergence: eyesim selects the first duplicate, drops unmatched focal rows and returns one for identical constant Pearson inputs; eyes4s preserves explicit ambiguity, missing-selection and undefined-correlation results.

cases.estimand: A seeded finite sample of eligible controls with the realized candidate set and denominator retained.
conventions: sampling without replacement distinguished from exhaustive enumeration
cases.independent_case: A cap of one over the two eligible controls detects priority, target-exclusion and denominator errors.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned finite-cap selection results without asserting cross-language PRNG identity unless the algorithm is shared.

cases.estimand: Explicit within-participant, across-occasion same-stimulus mean minus different-stimulus control mean; contrasted with the reference phase-only grouping across all participants and stimuli.
conventions: supplied normalized duration maps on a two-by-two grid, not KDE
reference denominators five/six; reinstatement denominators one/two
duplicate, singleton and empty reference output retained
cases.independent_case: Rational dot products and exhaustive participant/stimulus/occasion predicates determine both reference and reinstatement pairs and means independently. Finite-cap controls retain eligibility and nesting; the saved exhaustive two-phase route agrees per focal key.
cases.divergence: The reference phase-only condition groups across participants and stimuli, retaining duplicated rows; the reinstatement facade requires same participant, different occasion and explicit stimulus match/control roles, and excludes ambiguous full keys. These are documented different estimands, not a claim that every phase-only use is erroneous.

cases.estimand: For each focal trial, comparisons to same-condition and different-condition trials under an explicit participant and identity relation.
cases.independent_case: Exhaustive Cartesian pair enumeration detects reference join, self-edge and denominator defects.
cases.planned_evidence: Extend the verified supplied-map cosine case to the remaining methods and multiscale mean/none behavior; persist arbitrary all-occasion projections and finite-cap controls without changing their estimand.

cases.estimand: A labelled result at every requested bandwidth, optionally reduced by an explicit scale-weighted policy.
cases.independent_case: The 60-digit three-scale oracle detects sigma reuse and silent scale collapse, but intentionally does not claim eyesim KDE parity.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned eyesim scale-labelled output on a non-symmetric edge case and explicit unequal-scale failures.

cases.estimand: Matched-minus-control similarity between clipped duration-weighted fixation masses within named half-open windows.
conventions: fixation duration clipped to observed support
empty windows yield explicit absent contrasts
event weighting is distinct from sample weighting
backend_dependencies: no R backend; independent Python decimal oracle
cases.independent_case: Integer interval intersections establish every retained and missing duration before 60-digit cosine calculation.
cases.divergence: This eyes4s workflow estimates and compares window-specific duration mass. eyesim sample_density_time evaluates one static template density along an interpolated fixation trajectory, so the two outputs answer different temporal questions.

cases.estimand: Static template-density values evaluated along an interpolated focal fixation trajectory at requested times and optionally aggregated into bins.
conventions: bin closure and final-bin policy explicit
missing trajectory or template support retained
cases.independent_case: A two-fixation piecewise trajectory over a 2 by 2 template has hand-computable endpoint and midpoint values.
cases.planned_evidence: Pinned sample_density_time output and a separate eyes4s point-sampling plan.

cases.estimand: Held-out trial predictions from intercept-free OLS on predeclared fixed features, fitted from training rows only; distinct from eyesim's separate per-source normalized-map cell regression.
conventions: typed unique trial keys and explicit disjoint fold partitions
training-only CSV is distinct from the saved full recipe
QR rank tolerance 1e-7; singular/underdetermined designs refused
no learned feature construction or normalization
no coefficient standard errors or p-values
cases.independent_case: Exact rational normal equations give coefficients 1 and 2 and held-out prediction 7. Replacing only the held-out response by 700 leaves the exported training request and prediction unchanged. Deliberately including that row in fitting instead gives 701/8 and 709/8. The public eyesim normalized-map call returns 0.4 and 0.6 on the corresponding vectors.
cases.divergence: eyesim template_multireg normalizes each response/predictor map and fits over cells separately per source row. The new explicit recipe fits raw fixed features across training trials and evaluates held-out trials. The resulting coefficient bases and statistical units differ; neither this route nor the map reference establishes template_similarity_cv learned-transform parity.

cases.estimand: Held-out trial predictions from a model whose features, responses and fitted parameters are constructed from training folds only.
conventions: basic baseline fit is intercept-free lm
rlm, nnls and logistic may be deferred with explicit status
eyes4s_public_api: PredictorSet and learned training-only feature construction planned
cases.independent_case: The exact y=x1+2*x2 fit and a held-out response changed from 7 to 700 detect training/test leakage.
cases.planned_evidence: Extend the delivered fixed-feature no-intercept route to actual training-only learned feature/template construction and pinned template_similarity_cv/template_regression workflows. Surface decomposition must preserve Signed/Intensity/Mass types; robust and NNLS variants remain deferred, and binomial regression on continuous mass is excluded.

cases.estimand: One typed row per retained comparison or contrast key, carrying method identity, units, denominator, failure state and provenance.
conventions: base R can consume the exported file
cases.independent_case: Portable tests round-trip quoted keys, large microsecond values, failures and structured components; base R checks the emitted Scala CSV.
cases.divergence: eyesim returns mutable R data frames and list columns. eyes4s returns typed results and explicit versioned CSV or JSON schemas; the exported scientific values are checked where reference targets exist.

methods: all supported scalar and structured comparisons
cases.estimand: Reusable rows for every supported baseline output with complete scientific and execution provenance.
cases.independent_case: A schema audit requires every result variant, including failures and structured scores, to preserve its identifying columns.
cases.planned_evidence: Base-R consumption checks for each completed baseline workflow and JVM-only Arrow evidence under io-export.

methods: moment-matched affine: sqrt(reference covariance) times inverse sqrt(source covariance)
isotropic contraction from the covariance trace ratio
bilinear density resampling under the fitted map
out_of_baseline.estimand: A density-space map fitted from matched reference/source density moments within fit_by strata and applied to source density objects by resampling; not a coordinate transform.
conventions: fitted on eye_density or density objects, never on coordinates
training-only fitting per stratum with optional unique matching
coordinate tables are rejected, as the pinned fixture records
eyes4s_public_api: none: pure modules carry no fitting backend
out_of_baseline.independent_case: The pinned fixture records eyesim's response to coordinate tables; a future density-object case needs matched density moments computed independently of both implementations.
out_of_baseline.planned_evidence: Pinned R output for affine_transform and contract_transform on density objects with independently computed moment-matched maps, delivered through a typed optional adapter or an export/reimport recipe.
out_of_baseline.reason: fitted density-space maps belong with PCA, CORAL and CCA in a later adapter module; owner decision 2026-09-18
